newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sydkraft to demand compensation from gov't.
newsitem.headline: Sydkraft to demand compensation from gov't.

text.p: Swedish power company Sydkraft AB, the owner of the Barseback nuclear power plant, said on Monday it would demand full compensation from the government if a decision to phase out nuclear power affected the company.

"In the event of a possible phase out of nuclear power that affects Sydkraft, Sydkraft will, as it said earlier, demand full compensation," Sydkraft Managing Director Goran Ahlstrom said in a statement.
It said the compensation demanded would not be money.
"But in the form of the same quantity of electricity production at current costs and environmental effects, including a license for operation of these activities," he said.
He said such a nuclear power phase out could have serious consequences for its shareholders.
"This means difficult consequences for Sydkraft and its owners, of which a significant part are foreign companies."
Ahlstrom said that a phase out not deriving from safety reasons will mean that Sydkraft can get compensation based on Swedish constitutional law and European conventions.

The Social Democrats, the Centre Party and the Left Party agreed in the wee hours of Monday to begin phasing out nuclear power, Swedish radio said. Sources told the radio they agreed to close the Barseback nuclear plant just across from Denmark.
